question: What do the pinned AER LBLRTM/LNFL/line-file/MT_CKD sources establish about negative monochromatic total optical depth in this CO2 line-mixing diagnostic, and what independent reference would be defensible?
execution_policy: Read-only source and documentation review. No compile, line-file generation, solver, raw-file scan, model, or contact with maintainers was performed for this audit.

lblrtm_release_source.note: Instrumented candidate source copy; not byte-identical to the local stock build source or proven byte-identical to upstream commit a85ac734.

nocpl_continuum_enabled_sensitivity.comparison_scope: Plan states same ICNTNM=1 deck/profile as CPL continuum baseline; TAPE3 generated with LNFL NOCPL is the intended coupling-off change.

local_lblrtm.finding: HIRAC1 forms temperature-adjusted line strength SP, then SPPI=SUI*YI*PAVP0 and SPPSP=SPPI/SP. YI can therefore contribute a signed pressure-scaled term.

CNVFNV adds a base R3 contribution, then applies a separate coupling correction scaled by SPPSP. The implementation contains signed correction arithmetic; this source fact neither validates nor invalidates a negative sum at a given point.

local_lnfl.finding: The documented NOCPL control removes line-coupling data from TAPE3/TAPE7. Thus its reduction in negative samples demonstrates sensitivity to the coupling configuration; it does not establish that the coupled result is physically wrong or that the no-coupling result is more accurate.

primary_sources.title: AER LBLRTM code and data page
primary_sources.claim: AER says line coupling was used in deriving the CO2 continuum and must be used for accurate calculations with that continuum; the coupling parameters are carried in the AER line file.

primary_sources.title: AER-RC/LBLRTM README
primary_sources.claim: The official compatibility table pairs LBLRTM v12.17 with MT_CKD 4.3 and line file v3.8.1. The repository recommends the v12.17 release tag.

primary_sources.title: AER-RC/LBLRTM pinned release commit
primary_sources.claim: The official v12.17 release commit and its release metadata.

primary_sources.title: AER-RC/LNFL README
primary_sources.claim: LNFL converts the ASCII line database into LBLRTM TAPE3; NOCPL suppresses all line-coupling information on TAPE3/TAPE7.

primary_sources.title: AER FAQ, section 5.9
primary_sources.claim: Coupling parameters for O2, CO2, and CH4 come from the AER line database and are written to TAPE3 by LNFL.

primary_sources.title: AER-RC/LBLRTM issue tracker search
primary_sources.claim: A targeted public issue search did not surface a directly matching negative-total-OD/CO2-coupling report. This limited search is not evidence that no such report exists.

conclusions.matched_release_stack: The coupled line-only and coupled continuum runs use the local AER v3.8.1 line data/TAPE3 provenance; official AER lists the compatible LBLRTM v12.17 / MT_CKD 4.3 release pairing. The NOCPL continuum sensitivity uses a separate NOCPL-generated TAPE3 and is not a matched-physics reference.
conclusions.no_coupling_control: The controlled NOCPL comparison is ICNTNM=1 for both arms, with an identical TAPE5 and profile; only TAPE3 is regenerated with NOCPL. It reduces the negative count substantially, but is not a truth oracle. AER explicitly warns that coupling was used to derive the CO2 continuum, so coupling-off with continuum-on is specifically not the recommended accurate stack.
conclusions.historical_continuum_version: The selected coupled ICNTNM=0 line-only run has no continuum contribution. For the separate ICNTNM=1 paired comparison, the official compatible stack is MT_CKD 4.3 with LBLRTM v12.17 / AER line v3.8.1; do not use older 4.1 example artifacts as equivalent. The local NOCPL continuum arm is an intentional altered-physics sensitivity.
conclusions.physical_status: OPEN. These documents and source establish the configured algorithm and a relevant sensitivity, but do not establish whether the observed negative total OD at the selected samples is physically admissible, a coding defect, or a reference-data issue.
conclusions.next_discriminating_step: Use the matched release stack with coupling retained and independently validated published/reference spectra or benchmark cases. Any continuum-enabled check should be separately labeled and use the officially paired MT_CKD 4.3 data. Preserve strict numerical gates; do not treat NOCPL or an older 4.1 case as the truth reference.
